recap.text: Tish leaves a note for Ghazi stating the Gate of the Feral Gods can defeat Scolopendra. Holger and Clint fight with their fists to settle a debate about a nine-tier attack and soul gems. A moving mosaic on a ballroom ceiling shows a black centipede twisting around an upside-down white tree.

The AI introduces the Reminiscence Hydra, a level 125 City Boss with nine heads. Each head has the likeness of someone the crawlers know. The AI notes that in the third and fourth seasons, a bigger version served as a final boss and everyone died before getting close.

Carl examines War Leader Arief, a Semeru dwarf in feathered armour, and learns his people dug toward the goddess Ysalte until they struck the roots of the All Tree. Scolopendra's nine-tier attack left fewer than 10,000 Semeru alive. A System Message warns that Scolopendra stirs. Guests must reach a Motel 6 mirror in Boise, Idaho, by passing through the Backstage Death Maze.

Scolopendra, a brown-and-red centipede the size of an aircraft carrier, acts as a hotel for rich people and spews world-ending spells. Carl requests her arrival, and she begins a Nine-Tier Attack, starting with the Ox. A banger sphere carrying an enriched pet biscuit turns the level 500 boss into a puddle of goo. She reforms as a human-sized centipede with giant lips and a red bow, joining Carl's party as Crawler #12,953,456.

beats.headline: Tish's note
beats.text: According to the note Tish left for Ghazi, the Gate of the Feral Gods was the artifact needed to defeat Scolopendra.
beats.gist: Tish's note to Ghazi names the Gate of the Feral Gods as the artifact to defeat Scolopendra.

beats.headline: What the were-castors remember
beats.text: Holger's village came through the demon's cloud better than the city across the river, and he wonders if it was because one of the attacks in it was a transfiguration spell they had already been hit with. He got sick that day, and then was fine. Clint has it from the poem: the high elves cowered in their castle, protected by something they took. Rumour says they went down while she slept, collected their soul gems, and stole an item that shielded everyone in the castle. Holger thinks her nine-tier attack was a slow damage reflect. They settle it with their fists.
beats.gist: Holger and Clint fight with their fists to settle a disagreement about high elf soul gems.

beats.headline: Dreaming on the ballroom ceiling
beats.text: The ballroom's domed ceiling is a moving mosaic: a black-and-gold cave glittering with crystals, like the inside of a geode, and curled in it a black centipede that twists like a hypnotist's spiral. The note says this is Scolopendra, dreaming, and that when she finally awakens she will destroy everything and free us all. From the middle of the mosaic a living white tree hangs upside down, and the centipede never stops twisting around it, as if to strangle it.
beats.gist: A dreaming black centipede named Scolopendra twists around an upside-down white tree on a mosaic ceiling.

beats.headline: The hydra's old name
beats.text: The AI introduces the Reminiscence Hydra as a classic monster from the very early days of the show: in the third and fourth seasons, a bigger version was built as the final boss of the whole dungeon, and everybody died before getting close. In the old days these things were called Scolopendra Nymphs. That is not entirely accurate, the AI says, so this one goes by a different name. It is a level 125 City Boss with nine heads, each the likeness of somebody the crawlers know.
beats.gist: The AI introduces the nine-headed Reminiscence Hydra, a level 125 City Boss.

beats.headline: What the Semeru dug into
beats.text: Carl examines War Leader Arief, a young Semeru dwarf in feathered, parade-ready armour, and the System tells his people's story. They farmed and mined a paradise inside the volcano and dug toward the goddess below them, Ysalte, until they struck the roots of the All Tree and stopped. They built their castle along those roots, a monument and an apology. Scolopendra's nine-tier attack hit them hardest of all: millions before that day, fewer than 10,000 now. Arief is Despondent, because his goddess is dead.
beats.gist: Carl examines War Leader Arief, a Semeru dwarf in feathered armour, and learns the System's story.

beats.headline: Scolopendra Stirs, mid-council
beats.text: The warlord council has barely got going, just after the new king has punched the host, when a System Message cuts across the table: Warning: Scolopendra Stirs. Everyone goes quiet, even Ferdinand. Has that ever happened before, Carl asks. No, the Dream's warlord answers. Cascadia laughs with a hint of madness to it. Well, why not? Why the fuck not?
beats.gist: A System Message warns that Scolopendra Stirs during a warlord council, silencing everyone including Ferdinand.

beats.headline: Scolopendra has awakened
beats.text: The Nothing drains into the Halls of the Ascendency, into Sheol, and into Scolopendra's lair, and Scolopendra stirs. A planetwide message follows: guests of the Scolopendra Club should evacuate. Nowhere to go? The 16th floor, supposedly Agony of Mirrors, is an empty room with one non-magical mirror from a Motel 6 in Boise, Idaho, and it lies outside the Scolopendra layers. To reach it, guests must get through the 17th, the Backstage Death Maze, which is built and running. Good luck. Then: Scolopendra has awakened.
beats.gist: The Nothing drains into the Halls of the Ascendency, Sheol, and Scolopendra's lair, awakening Scolopendra.

beats.headline: Awake, and moving
beats.text: Scolopendra is awake. So far it has done nothing but move around a lot, which is plenty when there is a club inside it. The guests of the resort on the eighteenth floor cannot eject, and the system brings them straight back each time they die. Things leaked out of the broken Nothing, forgotten gods and demons from hundreds of old quests among them, and some are appearing inside the boss, inside the club, among guests who cannot die no matter what is done to them. The cameras went dark after the first few hours.
beats.gist: Scolopendra moves around while guests who cannot eject or die stay inside its club.

beats.headline: One of three children
beats.text: Rosetta's version, told in the pet stables: before the current pantheon there were older gods, and Nekhebit, a vulture, was forbidden children and had three. Apito. A son. And a centipede, which is Scolopendra. Sometimes Scolopendra is the Scavenger, and the Scavenger's Daughter comes of its union with someone else; sometimes the son is; sometimes all three are one being, split. Elle's summary is that the centipede became a hotel for rich people that spews world-ending spells from the bottom of the dungeon. It is not a bad summary.
beats.gist: Rosetta tells Elle in the pet stables that Scolopendra is a forbidden child of Nekhebit.

beats.headline: The first of nine attacks
beats.text: System Message: Scolopendra has released the first of nine attacks. The quest is called the Nine-Tier Attack. The first four are temporary and survivable, and this first one has a twenty per cent chance of landing on anyone unprotected. At least thirty hours between them, unless she is confronted or upset, and then they come fast. A wheel of nine symbols spins in the lobby and lands on the Ox: the Beast of Burden Sin, Transformation. For crawlers, it lasts until the next stairwell.
beats.gist: Scolopendra releases the first of nine attacks, and the wheel lands on the Ox.

beats.headline: The Dungeon boss, and its rules
beats.text: Scolopendra arrives at Carl's request: level 500, the final boss of the dungeon, a plain brown-and-red centipede the size of an aircraft carrier. The AI spells out the rules. Kill her and the level timers cease, only one more round of deals is offered, and the Ascendency battles begin, with the dungeon collapsing twelve hours after a winner is crowned. Leave her on a collapsing floor and nobody can exit. Either way, killing or abandoning her triggers every remaining attack of the nine at once.
beats.gist: Scolopendra, a brown-and-red centipede the size of an aircraft carrier, arrives at Carl's request.

beats.headline: A biscuit down the throat
beats.text: A banger sphere carrying an enriched pet biscuit, thrown into her open mouth as the third attack spins up, and the level 500 Dungeon boss splatters onto the arena floor as a quivering puddle of goo. Uzi Jesus, firing his toy gun at the heap, reports a lot of people's auras inside it.
beats.gist: A banger sphere with an enriched pet biscuit splatters the level 500 boss into goo.

beats.headline: A new member has joined your party
beats.text: The heap drains away and leaves a human-sized centipede: armless, twin yellow antennae with a red bow on one, a humanlike face with strangely giant lips. Not a pet. Sexy Scolopendra, level 1, Crawler #12,953,456, in Carl's party. The warning stands: kill her, even now, or abandon her on any floor, and the remaining attacks go off at once. She wraps herself around Carl and suggests the portal before the collapse. Boop.
beats.gist: A human-sized centipede named Sexy Scolopendra joins Carl's party.

beats.headline: The myth, read in the original
beats.text: Sydnee Iglacia, on Danger Zone: in the earliest translations the nine-tier attack is not nine spells. Some attacks are social, rapid shifts in philosophy. The first is control of infrastructure. The second is A Parade of Horribles, when people learn what is happening and panic sets in; the third, This Inevitable Ruin, when they accept their fate and turn on one another; the fourth, Bedlam. In the fairy tale a princess kills the all-tree to temper the final attack, and everyone she loves with it.
beats.gist: Sydnee Iglacia explains that the nine-tier attack includes social shifts, infrastructure control, and people turning on one another.

relations.note: The digging that woke her, in the legend
One of the three children she was forbidden
